text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Police are puzzled as to how a tour bus with 23 holiday-makers from Singapore could ram into the rear of a lorry parked on the emergency lane near Nilai despite the presence of luminous warning markers and cones. Thirteen were killed, and 12 injured in the accident.

- Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia will be accused of "moral corruption" if pockets of poverty still exist in a larger propering society -- pointing out that one of the capital's squatter areas is only 15 minutes away from his Finance Ministry office.

- Malaysia Mining Corp Bhd has pulled out of the Bakun hydroelectric project in Sarawak. Khazanah Holdings Bhd, the government's investment arm, will take up MMC's five percent equity in the 13.02 billion ringgit project.

- A new world in the 21st century must be characterised by "liberte, egalite and fraternite" and one that is populated by flourishing, responsible and productive democracies, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said.

- The market supervision department of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange handled a total of 327 cases this year relating to the potential breaches of trading and reporting rules by market intermediaries and to tampered, lost or destroyed share certificates.
- Thirteen Singaporeans were killed and 12 others injured when their tour bus burst into flames after crashing into a stationary lorry on the emergency lane of the North-South Expressway near Bangi.

- Ekran Bhd, the developer of the 13.6 billion ringgit Bakun hydroelectric dam project in central Sarawak, has formally handed over the construction work for the main dam to the multinational consortium chosen to handle the project.
